newsitem.title: CHINA: China says not exploiting restive Xinjiang region.
newsitem.headline: China says not exploiting restive Xinjiang region.

text.p: China has dismissed reports it is exploiting its restive far-western region of Xinjiang, saying shipments of oil from the mainly Moslem area were a vital support to the local economy.
The official Xinhua news agency, in a report late on Wednesday, quoted a spokesman of the State Planning Commission as saying that resources found in the vast region were mostly used locally.

A report forwarded by the United Nations Centre for Human Rights had accused China of forcing Xinjiang to give the central government 80 million tonnes of oil and 40 million tonnes of grain under the current five-year plan ending in the year 2000, Xinhua said.
The agency said Xinjiang processed and used locally most of the 14 million tonnes of crude oil it produced in 1996, with only the remainder sold to other regions.
The sale of oil to other areas not only supported the whole country but also met the needs of local economic development, the spokesman said, adding such actions were beyond reproach.
State grain purchases from Xinjiang were made in the interest of the region's farmers and reports claiming otherwise were distortions prompted by ulterior motives, he said.

Chinese officials regularly accuse "Western forces" of trying to split China by supporting separatists in Xinjiang, which has been rocked by a spate of bombings and assassinations by pro-independence activists in recent years.

A series of bombs killed nine and wounded 74 in the region's capital of Urumqi last month. Exiled separatists have claimed responsibility and vowed to stage further attacks until they gain their own state of East Turkestan.

Beijing had long poured investment and other support into Xinjiang and had done everything it could to support development among the ethnic minorities that dominate the region's population, Xinhua said.

"For quite some time, some people in the international community, in the name of protecting human rights, have been maliciously attacking China and sowing dissension among Chinese nationalities with fabricated and distorted cases," it said.
"Their plot will never succeed," it quoted the spokesman as saying.
